AddMemory.description: Create a new memory (item + first revision).
AddMemory.title: AddMemory

rationale.description: Why: what you saw that makes this change right
rationale.title: Rationale

ConceptDefinition.description: Request: create a concept. The id is derived from the label.
ConceptDefinition.title: ConceptDefinition

DuplicateCluster.description:
Memories that say the same thing. `keep` is the oldest; the rest can be superseded by it
(or the other way round) with an ordinary proposal; a human or agent decides.
DuplicateCluster.title: DuplicateCluster

Evidence.description: A source episode; if `quote` is given it must literally occur in that episode.
Evidence.title: Evidence

Finding.description: One validation observation. `error` blocks the proposal; others are advice.
Finding.title: Finding

IssuedCredential.description: The only time the token is ever shown.
IssuedCredential.title: IssuedCredential

MemoryDetail.description: `get` with optional expansions (history, links, evidence, applicability).
MemoryDetail.title: MemoryDetail

Proposal.description: An atomic batch of operations submitted by one actor (see plans/01, plans/10).
Proposal.title: Proposal

RecallContext.description: Where and in what circumstances the agent is working. All parts are optional.
RecallContext.title: RecallContext

RerankerRun.description: One training run of a reranker: what went in, how it did, whether it was activated.
RerankerRun.title: RerankerRun

ResolveRequest.description:
Ask the daemon to do what the card proposes (as a proposal from you): `merge` keeps the
oldest memory of a duplicate cluster and supersedes the others; `supersede` lets the newer
memory of an update replace the older; `retract` retracts the memory of a feedback or expiry
task.
ResolveRequest.title: ResolveRequest

Resource.description:
A registered anchor. Containment is mostly syntactic (path segments); this record adds
explicit containment (`parents`) and equivalence (`same_as`) on top (plans/01).
Resource.title: Resource

RetractMemory.description: Declare a memory wrong/polluted. Dependents derived from it are flagged stale.
RetractMemory.title: RetractMemory

ReviseMemory.description: New revision of an existing memory; `fields` overlay the current revision.
ReviseMemory.title: ReviseMemory

Signal.description: An observation about the environment, by concept id or label ("python", 3.12).
Signal.title: Signal

SupersedeMemory.description: `new` (a `ref` from this proposal, or an existing memory id) replaces `target`.
SupersedeMemory.title: SupersedeMemory

SupersessionReason.description: Why a revision was replaced (the `supersedes` edge's own fields).
SupersessionReason.title: SupersessionReason

TaskResult.description:
How a maintenance task was resolved. `merge` (a duplicate cluster), `supersede` (an
update), `retract` and `revise` (a memory reported wrong or expiring) must cite the proposal
that did it; `distinct` (two memories differ) and `keep` (the memory stands) are remembered and
not raised again; `defer` parks the task for later.
TaskResult.title: TaskResult

UpdateCandidate.description:
The same statement with a changed value (a version, an amount, a date): `newer` probably
supersedes `older`. Not a duplicate: merging would lose the update.
UpdateCandidate.title: UpdateCandidate

info.description:
Structured, typed memory for agents. Writes go through **proposals** (validated, then
committed or held for review by policy); reads return current memories with their history.

Authentication: off by default (run on localhost only; the caller is then a label from
`X-Ontyra-Actor`, `X-Ontyra-Actor-Kind`, `X-Ontyra-Harness`). With `ONTYRA_AUTH__TOKEN` every
request needs `Authorization: Bearer <token>`. With `ONTYRA_AUTH__MULTI_USER` each account has
credentials (see `/v1/admin`); the account decides the owner, actor kind and permissions, and
the headers are ignored. An owner is never a request parameter.
info.title: Ontyra

post.description: The only way to write memories. A proposal is an all-or-nothing batch of operations (`add`, `revise`, `supersede`, `retract`, `link`, `annotate`). It is validated, then the commit policy decides: **201** committed, **202** held for review, **422** rejected (the body lists the findings). Warnings and info findings are advice, e.g. a possible duplicate you may want to supersede.
